Gods, goddesses, those knowing, those unknowable, those that are perpendicular to the world, yet form the axis upon which it turns. Welcome.

You doubtless know of the invasion. Even now it swarms on the horizon. A pulsing blackening, an expanding blight.

Phyra extends his tendrils.

He is not content to build and guide. He is not willing to share and be shared with, to shape and advance by degrees, to take his role in the foundation of the universe, as we all have. He does not wish to join in the gentle tug-of-war that is the constant struggle to be first among equals.

This is because he does not see us as equals.

In Phyra's mind, there can only be one world. His world. A world in which he and his exist, and the rest of us and ours, are meaningless. Or gone entirely.

We have wrought a complex web, together, here in this void. Stars and moons, tides and stones. Each of us has extended love into this tapestry, in his , her, their own way. The threads tangle at times; At times we are at odds. But from these tangles grow new, beautiful patterns, the likes of which none of us alone could have imagined. Perhaps I'm biased. I adore the consequence of conflict. Forgive me this conceit. But look! Look upon your pattern. Upon your world. See that it is beautiful, in its myriad differences!

Phyra does not wish to tangle. Phyra does not wish to weave. Phyra would throw the tapestry aside, save those few threads here and there that please him, and banish us from the loom.

I know I am biased. I know not all of you will find the cessation of so many individual struggles, the premature conclusion of so many histories, the making moot of so many victories, as offensive, as utterly distateful, as I do. Nor should you. We each have our own concerns.

But there is a deeper offence here. A lack, fundamentally, of *respect.* Not for the races. Not for the struggles. A lack of respect for *you.* For *us.*

Phyra sees a a work of the gods, born of creation and compromise, grown over eons, accepted by most, and dashes it into the dirt, so that it may never be seen.

Phyra sees a god impose a set of values, a set of values which are not his but are nevertheless *fundamental,* so fundamental as to require a god, every bit as fundamental as his, and would rip those values from the world entirely.

Phyra would, by these actions, declare himself superior. A master of what must and must not be. Not equal, not even first among equals, but despot and ruler.

I ask you. Do you bow to Phyra? Do you cede this world entirely to him, and his will? Do you allow him to deny and destroy the very gods themselves, and assert that his nature is somehow worthier, superior? That he is a god worth many gods? Are we to be, from now on, his plaything, our works to be plucked away whenever he is displeased?

Or do we show him, once and for all, that while he is fundamental, so, too, are we all?

We must discuss this, friends and fellows. For yes, even those that I struggle against, I consider friends and fellows. Even Phyra! Who moves now to mistreat me so. Even him, I value, as an important part, and in our collective great work, an important ally.

A part.

Not the whole.
